title: Comparing References
goal: Understand that comparison operators on references compare values.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 4 Afternoon: Standard Traits

hints: Rust's == operator automatically dereferences references to invoke `PartialEq::eq`.
Both sides of == must have matching reference types.
explanation: When `==` is used on references `&u1 == &u2`, Rust dereferences them and calls `PartialEq::eq`, comparing underlying values. Using `u1 == &u2` causes type mismatch `E0308`. Dereferencing `*u1` fails with `E0614` because `u1` is a value, not a reference. JavaScript's `===` operator is not valid Rust syntax.
